summary: The missions and work list refreshers publish at one cut through a burst of changes instead of giving up and keeping the previous publication.

replay.detail: No replay trigger or recovery wait. The lists are in-memory publications folded from the existing projections.

schema.detail: No tables, columns, indexes or migrations.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule, registry or coordinated member upgrade change.

compatibility.detail: The published rows are the ones the direct read gives at the publication's cut, as before; only how a fold catches up changes. Nothing is written, replicated or sent differently, so mixed-version fleets with the previous release interoperate unchanged. A fold's last catch-up round now refolds every row still changed in one read snapshot, so during a burst that snapshot can refold more than the usual 100 rows.

downtime.detail: No storage migration or added startup work.

manual.detail: Nothing to configure. A refresher's 'kept changing in ways no short fold can follow' line now appears only when a catch-up round must fold from nothing: more than 10,000 claims to read since the provisional cut, or, for the work list, a replica repair since it.

recovery.detail: An older build goes back to giving up after three chunked rounds; nothing is stored.
